idea-plugin.name: spek - OpenSpec Viewer
idea-plugin.description:
spek is an OpenSpec content viewer that lets you browse specs, changes, and task progress directly within your IDE.

Features:

  • Specs Browser — Browse spec documents with BDD syntax highlighting (WHEN/GIVEN, THEN, AND, MUST/SHALL)
  • Changes Browser — View changes with a tab per artifact the change contains (custom OpenSpec schemas supported), with the change's schema shown as a badge; rows surface creation/archive dates and lifecycle duration
  • Timeline — Horizontal Gantt-style chart of every change's lifecycle, with optional spec-topic grouping and an auto-scaling time axis
  • Task Progress — Track task completion with section-grouped progress bars
  • Graph View — Interactive force-directed graph showing spec-change relationships
  • Full-text Search — Search across all specs and changes
  • Spec Diff — Compare current spec content against historical change versions
  • Live Reload — Automatically refreshes when openspec files change on disk
  • Collapsible Tree Navigator — A Specs / Changes tree sits above the viewer. Hide it from the tool window title bar or the gear menu to give the viewer the whole tool window; the choice and the split ratio are remembered per project
  • Dark / Light Theme — Syncs with your IDE theme

Supported IDEs: IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, PhpStorm, GoLand, RubyMine, CLion, Rider, and other IntelliJ-based IDEs (2023.3+)

Getting Started: Open a project that contains an openspec/ directory. The spek tool window will appear in the right sidebar.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.15.0

The schema workflow diagram now says which steps come after implementation — and its lines can finally be seen. OpenSpec has no way to declare "this artifact is produced once the change is implemented": an artifact's requires may name only other artifacts, so authors point such a step at the last planning artifact and state the real ordering in prose. spek rendered the declared graph faithfully, which put those steps on apply's own level, reading as its peers.

  • A step that follows implementation is drawn after apply, on a dashed edge captioned as spek's inference. The ordering is derived from the requires graph and is never drawn like a declared one, because openspec status does not block on it. Of the 88 OpenSpec schemas discoverable on GitHub, 18 declare such a step. Thanks to @nthansen (Norman Hansen), PR #48.
  • apply is a real node in the flow now, so the steps after it hang off it and archive follows the tail. A schema that declares an artifact literally named apply no longer collapses into the apply phase — both are separate, selectable steps.
  • A derived edge is explained once, and never erases a dependency the CLI enforces. Where a declared path already implies the ordering the derived edge is dropped; where the reverse held, an inference used to imply a real requires away.
  • An edge no longer detours through the node it exists to go around. Two edges converging on one step were ordered by the other end's column alone, so a tie put the long way round on the inside slot.
  • Every line in the diagram is visible in both themes. Edges, arrowheads, the archive step's dashed outline and both legend swatches were drawn in the panel-hairline colour — 1.22:1 dark and 1.13:1 light at full strength. They now measure 5.52:1 and 5.17:1.
  • A selected step's generates label is readable — over the accent wash a selected step draws it measured 4.45:1 in the light theme.
  • A graph node's label stays readable whichever node is drawn next to it. The halo behind each label was painted inside its own node's group, so it survived only the collisions with nodes drawn before it.
  • An unreadable response from the OpenSpec CLI is treated as a failure, not as an answer. An exit-0 run whose output could not be parsed was cached as "this schema has no artifact order" for the full cache window.
  • An installation that cannot answer the artifact-order query stops costing a process start per change. A refusal is now remembered against the change it was about, instead of being re-run on every open and every refresh.
